# Implement block: Expanding Filter Rows (Jetpack Compose)

You are adding the "Expanding Filter Rows" block from Native Cook to the user's Android app. The block already exists as working Kotlin code. Your job is to bring it into this project faithfully, not to write a new one that looks similar.

## The block

A dark "Filters" sheet with five rows, each a 60 pt rounded bar with a grey icon and label at the left and its value at the right: "Dates" with "18 Dec 2024", "Friends attend" with a small column of friends' pictures that take turns and "12+", "Time" with "7:00 pm", "Genres" with "Afrobeat, Bluegrass +6" and "Price" with "All price"; at the bottom "Reset all" and a blue pill "Continue with 4" over a fade that rows slide under. A tap on Time springs the row open, pushing the rows below it down, into a darker well with two options, "Single time" and "Time range", an analog clock and a wheel of times in half-hour steps: turning the wheel turns the clock's hands, and "Time range" slides a second wheel in, points the short hand at the start and the long one at the end, and draws a blue arc between them along the rim. A tap on Genres closes Time and opens two facing lists that lie on the rims of two big wheels, so the names tilt and fade away from the middle: the chosen genres on the left, the others with blue rings on the right; each list turns under the finger and a tap moves a genre across. The other rows change value on a tap, and the number on the button counts the filters that are set.

**Motion.** A row opens and shuts on a spring (damping 14.5, stiffness 115, mass 1, a few percent of overshoot): its height goes from 60 pt to 284 pt for Time and 302 pt for Genres while the well fades in between 10% and 70% of the way and drops 12 pt into place; in the Time well the options fade in from 15% to 60% and the clock and wheel from 45% to 100%, scaling up from 0.96. Opening one row shuts the other on the same spring, and an open row that would reach the bar's 44 pt fade slides the whole list up by the difference. A wheel line is 23 pt; a line is at 100% in the middle, 72% one line away, 32% two away and gone at 2.7. A drag turns the wheel one line per 23 pt (it gives a little past either end); on release it lands the velocity × 0.14 s ahead on a spring without bounce (damping 24, stiffness 190) and each line that passes the middle gives a selection haptic. With one time t (in half hours) the short hand stands at t × 15° and the long one at t × 180°, so one line is half a turn of the long hand. "Time range" takes 380 ms (ease-out cubic): the first wheel moves 48 pt left, the second fades in 28 pt further right and slides to 48 pt right, the long hand turns the shorter way round to the end time × 15°, and the 4 pt arc at radius 51 of the 118 pt clock runs from start to end (a dot when they are equal); a wheel turned past the other takes it along. The genre wheels have a radius of 280 pt and 7.5° between names (36.5 pt at the middle), the left hub far to the left with names right-aligned 24 pt left of the well's centre, the right hub far to the right with rings starting 27 pt right of it; a name is rotated by its angle about its end on the rim, fully lit within 1.2 names of the middle, 82% at 2, 32% at 3 and gone at 3.6. While the row opens the two wheels turn into place from 2.5 names away in opposite directions. A tapped genre fills its ring (140 ms, scale 1.25) and fades for 260 ms, then appears on the other wheel right under its middle name, fading in over 320 ms while the names around both gaps take their new places on a spring (damping 20, stiffness 210). Row values cross-fade (220 ms in, 140 ms out), the button's number rolls up (220 ms in from below, 160 ms out upward), a pressed row lightens in 60 ms and lets go in 260 ms, and a friend's picture gives way to the next every 3.5 s on a spring (damping 16, stiffness 150). The self-playing demo loops every 10.5 s with no haptics: Time is pressed at 0.8 s, "Time range" at 1.9 s, the start wheel is carried back five lines to 4:30 pm from 2.6 s over 1.2 s (ease-in-out cubic), Genres is pressed at 4.4 s, the right wheel is carried five names on from 5.4 s over 1 s, "Folk" is tapped at 6.9 s, Genres is pressed shut at 7.9 s and "Reset all" at 8.9 s puts every value back; a touch takes over and the loop resets and starts again 3 s later. Under reduced motion rows open in 160 ms without a spring and the pictures stay still. Native autoplay clears the wheels’ retained manual-haptic ownership before automatic assignments so a resumed tour stays silent; manual wheel reactions are retained.

## Reference source

The block is built and running in the Native Cook source repository. Each link below is a file on GitHub. To read one as plain text, replace `https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/` with `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/` in its address.

### Demo (start here)

- [ExpandingFilterRowsDemo.kt](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/kotlin/app/src/main/java/com/ngocdevv/nativecook/blocks/forms/expandingfilterrows/ExpandingFilterRowsDemo.kt)

### Files of the block

- [ExpandingFilterRows.kt](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/kotlin/app/src/main/java/com/ngocdevv/nativecook/blocks/forms/expandingfilterrows/ExpandingFilterRows.kt)
- [GenreDrum.kt](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/kotlin/app/src/main/java/com/ngocdevv/nativecook/blocks/forms/expandingfilterrows/GenreDrum.kt)
- [TimeDial.kt](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/kotlin/app/src/main/java/com/ngocdevv/nativecook/blocks/forms/expandingfilterrows/TimeDial.kt)

### Shared helpers the block uses

- [kotlin/app/src/main/java/com/ngocdevv/nativecook/shared/ComponentSupport.kt](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/kotlin/app/src/main/java/com/ngocdevv/nativecook/shared/ComponentSupport.kt)

### Libraries

It needs no library beyond a new Compose project.

## Your instructions

_Anything specific to this app goes here: where the block should appear, what to rename, what to change. Left empty, integrate the block as it is._

## How to work

Work like an experienced Android engineer joining an existing project: learn the app first, read only what you need, decide early how the block fits, then integrate it with as little disruption as possible. Take the steps in order.

**Done means** the block is reachable in the user's app and behaves like the reference on an emulator or a device. A Compose preview is useful while you work, but it is not the proof: build, install and run the app.

**Fidelity.** Bring over the real implementation. Keep its structure, colours, sizes, timings and easing. Change only what this project requires and what "Your instructions" ask for.

If you already learned this project earlier in the conversation, reuse what you know and skip step 2. Learn it again only if the project changed or something you need is missing.

### 1. Check where you are

- You need the project's files and a terminal. If this prompt was pasted into a chat that has neither, stop and say so: it has to be run by a coding agent opened on the project.
- Confirm the project is an Android app built with Gradle. If it is something else, stop, say what you found, and do not create a new app inside it unless the instructions ask for one.

### 2. Learn the host app

- The app module, its namespace, `minSdk`, `compileSdk`, and the versions of Kotlin, the Android Gradle Plugin and Compose (a BOM or single versions).
- Whether Compose is switched on in that module, and whether screens are Compose, Views or both.
- Navigation: Navigation Compose, fragments, activities, or a single screen. Find how a screen is added today.
- How dependencies are declared: a version catalog (`libs.versions.toml`) or directly in `build.gradle`.
- Conventions: package layout, naming, theme, where resources live and how they are named.

### 3. Read the block

- Open the demo, then each file in the block's package. The list above names every file of the block, and the resources it uses from outside its package.
- The demo is how the source repository shows the block. Bring over what the demo shows, not the repository's gallery. Anything listed under "Used by the demo only" stays behind.
- Read the block's parameters and their defaults. The demo may switch on an option that makes the block play by itself for a recording (for example `autoPlay`). Keep the option; leave it off in the user's app unless asked.

### 4. Decide the fit

- Compare the block's libraries and the versions it was built with to the host's. Add what is missing the way this project declares dependencies. Do not upgrade the host's Kotlin, Gradle plugin or Compose versions without asking; if an API differs on the host's version, adapt the block's code.
- Check `minSdk`. If the block uses an API newer than the host's minimum, keep the fallback the source has, or tell the user what would be lost.
- If Compose is not switched on in the module, say what turning it on involves before you do it. In a View-based screen, show the block through a `ComposeView`.
- Shared helpers: copy the ones the block imports next to it, or fold them into the block's files. Do not copy helpers it never calls.

### 5. Bring it in

- Copy the block's files into a package of this app, and rewrite the `package` lines and the imports, including the import of the app's own `R` class.
- Copy its resources and asset files. Keep their names unless one collides with a resource of the app; then rename it everywhere it is used.
- Keep reduced-motion handling, haptics and accessibility descriptions as they are in the source. If the block needs a permission, add it to the manifest and say so.
- Mount the block where the instructions say. With no instructions, add a screen or destination named after the block and make it reachable the way the app's other screens are.

### 6. Run it

- Build with the project's own task, for example `./gradlew :app:assembleDebug`, and fix every error and new warning the block introduced.
- Install and run it, and use the block: every state, every gesture, and once with animations switched off in the system settings.
- If the build or the emulator fails for a reason outside the block, report the error and ask how to continue.

### 7. Report

- Files added and changed, dependencies and permissions added, and anything renamed to avoid a collision.
- How to reach the block in the app.
- Anything that differs from the reference, and why.
